questions.q: Who is credited with founding the Delhi Sultanate in 1206 CE?
questions.a: Qutbuddin Aibak founded the Delhi Sultanate. A wrong answer suggests the student is confusing him with later rulers or the previous leader, Muhammad of Ghur, indicating they haven't distinguished between the founder and the predecessor.

questions.q: Why do historians call 1206 CE the start of the Delhi Sultanate?
questions.a: It is the year Qutbuddin Aibak declared himself independent ruler after his leader died. If a student says it's just a random date, they misunderstand that the Sultanate began with a specific political action of independence.

questions.q: Calculation: 1526 minus 1206 equals 320 years. A wrong answer reveals a struggle with basic chronological subtraction, which is vital for understanding historical timelines.
questions.a:
The Delhi Sultanate lasted for a total of 320 years. This is calculated by subtracting the starting year of 1206 from the ending year of 1526.

A wrong answer reveals that the student likely lacks the foundational skill of chronological subtraction or is struggling with the concept of "duration" in historical timelines, perhaps attempting to add the two years together instead of finding the difference between them.

questions.q: How did a "former slave" become a Sultan? What does this tell us about the society of that time?
questions.a: It shows that military skill and loyalty could lead to high positions regardless of birth status. A wrong answer suggests the student thinks only people born into royal families could lead, missing the point of Aibak's unique rise.

questions.q: Is it accurate to say the Delhi Sultanate was ruled by only one family for 300 years? Why or why not?
questions.a: No, it was ruled by five successive dynasties. A wrong answer indicates the student thinks "Sultanate" implies a single family line, missing the diversity of the five different groups that held power.

questions.q: Imagine you are a historian writing a headline for the year 1206 CE. What would it be?
questions.a: A good answer would mention "A New Era Begins" or "From General to Sultan." A poor answer is vague, like "The Sultanate happened," which fails to capture the significance of the transition.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: The Delhi Sultanate was the first major Islamic empire ______ in northern India, beginning in 1206 CE when Qutbuddin Aibak declared himself the independent ruler of Delhi.
Fill in the blank: Starting in 1206 CE, India experienced a similar change in "leadership" when a former general named ______ Aibak took charge of Delhi.
Fill in the blank: The Delhi Sultanate was the first major Islamic empire established in northern India, beginning in ______ CE when Qutbuddin Aibak declared himself the independent ruler of Delhi.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to identify Qutbuddin Aibak as the founder and explain that the Sultanate was a political change that lasted from 1206 to 1526 CE.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Starting in 1206 CE, India ______ a similar change in "leadership" when a former general named Qutbuddin Aibak took charge of Delhi.
